- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.36) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), true outcome often corrects downward within 7–10 days; apply lagged mean reversion to next 3–5 periods.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.18) and model forecasts are rising, model often overcorrects; cap upward forecasts at 1–2% above recent 5-day average.
- If true outcome exceeds model by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias correction for next 5 days (especially if sentiment is neutral or negative).
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model tends to underestimate when sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.18–0.53); use sentiment-weighted moving average to adjust baseline.
- If model forecast is below true outcome by >2% for 5+ days, model is underestimating trend; increase forecast by 0.5–1% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
